literal: Riding the palmyra horse, even at midnight, I will think of, surely; closing not agreeing, because of the beloved, my eyes.
translation: My eyes refuse to close in sleep because of my beloved; surely, even in the dead of night, I think only of riding the palmyra horse.
modern: என் கண்கள் அந்தப் பேதைக்காகத் தூங்குவதற்கு உடன்படவில்லை; அதனால், நள்ளிரவிலும் நான் மடல் ஊர்வதைப் பற்றியே நிச்சயமாக நினைப்பேன்.
explanation: The lover is suffering from sleeplessness because of his beloved, whom he refers to as 'pētai' (the innocent or simple girl). Since his eyes refuse to close (paṭal ollā) in sleep, he lies awake even during the dead of night (yāmattum). In this quiet, sleepless state, his mind is entirely and surely (maṉṟa) occupied with the thought of riding the palmyra horse (maṭalūrtal) to publicly declare his love and end his torment.
